decisions.decision: MVP is fully static (no backend/DB/auth/admin/checkout/analytics), architected with a repository + integrations layer so a backend (e.g. v2 WhatsApp AI bot) can be added later without rewriting the frontend
decisions.rationale: Client's explicit architecture requirement; minimizes attack surface for a showcase-only site

decisions.decision: iFood = primary order channel; WhatsApp = human-staffed secondary channel (not a bot) in the MVP
decisions.rationale: Client confirmed no AI bot exists today; bot deferred to v2 with mandatory new threat-model review (SEC-17) before implementation

decisions.decision: Stack: Next.js 16 (App Router) + React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind v4 + Zod-style build-time data validation
decisions.rationale: Confirmed as current best-fit by dedicated stack research; no better alternative found
Native next/image optimization (critical for LCP with food photography) + simplest CSP/HSTS header config, per research

decisions.decision: No live embedded Google Maps iframe or Instagram feed embed in the MVP — links/buttons only
decisions.rationale: Found during REQUIREMENTS.md client review: third-party embed scripts would make Lighthouse/CWV targets dependent on an external service's reliability

decisions.decision: REQUIREMENTS.md restructured into 5 explicit blocks at client's request: (1) mandatory MVP, (2) optional/v2, (3) security, (4a/4b automated-vs-operational acceptance criteria, (5) pending confirmations
decisions.rationale: Client wanted duplicates removed and testable criteria separated from process/operational checklist items

decisions.decision: Phase order re-sequenced from research's suggestion (Foundation → Menu → Hero/Location → Promotions → Verification) to Foundation → Hero/CTAs/Location → Menu/Catalog → Promotions/Almoço → SEO/Perf/Security
decisions.rationale: Matches client's stated launch gate ('hero + cardápio funcionando já é lançável') exactly — that pair must be phases 2+3, not scattered
